newsitem.title: INDIA: Investors "vanishing" from India IPO market - PRIME.
newsitem.headline: Investors "vanishing" from India IPO market - PRIME.

text.p: India's independent primary market monitor PRIME said an analysis of primary issues in 1995/96 (April-March) revealed an alarming absence of retail investors.
"As many as 1,191 or 86 percent of the total issues in 1995/96 managed to attract less than 5,000 investors each on an all-India basis," PRIME said in a statement.
PRIME said in the previous year only 36 percent of the 1,320 issues fared so badly while in 1993/94 20 percent of 746 issues met with a poor response.

"Worse, in 1995/96 as many as 287 issues (21 percent) could manage to convince less than even 500 investors each," PRIME said, adding its study clearly illustrated retail investors were moving away from India's primary market.

"While almost all small issues failed to impress the potential investors, there was no respite for the mega issues also which had undertaken extensive marketing efforts to reach out to and attract a large number of investing population," PRIME said.
The study showed only four of 12 issues of above one billion rupees attracted more than 100,000 investors each. These were IDBI-Bonds, IDBI-equity, Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam and Pal Peugeot.
"The only small issue to attract more than 100,000 investors was Maxworth Orchards whose 40.5 million rupee issue got 101,000 applications," PRIME said.
PRIME said the maximum number of applications in 1995/96 were attracted by bond issues from state-run companies like IDBI, ICICI, IRFC and Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam.
"Obviously the investors did not respond to equity issues any more, despite some excellent investment opportunities," PRIME said.
